2. Undisputedly, acquisition process was initiated on behalf of .
Larji Hydel Project for acquisition of land by issuing notification dated 29.10.2005 under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act (for short 'the Act'), wherein, alongwith other land, intention to acquire land of temple measuring 0-06-12 bighas compromised in Khasra No. 195, situated in Mohal Aut Tehsil Aut, District Mandi was notified and thereafter Notification under Section 6 of the Act was issued in furtherance to notification under Section 4 of the Act.

On completion of acquisition proceedings, Land Acquisition Collector under Sections 11 of the Act vide award No. 303 dated 21.3.2007 has determined the value of land and structure thereon, and awarded the compensation to the land owners including the appellant herein with specific details of above referred land as well as Khasra number.

3. It is also undisputed that being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the award passed by Land Acquisition Collector, appellants alongwith land owners had preferred Reference Petitions under Section 18 of the Act for enhancement which, except the Reference Petition of the appellant, have been allowed by giving enhancement of 10% to the value of structure, but without enhancing the value of land determined by Land Acquisition Collector.
4. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and also gone through the record.

5. To the Reference Petition preferred by the appellant, reply was filed on behalf of respondents and in the said reply there is specific stand of the respondents that value of compensation as determined by Land Acquisition Collector is justified and appellants are not entitled for any enhanced amount of compensation.
There is not even a whisper that Temple or Inn or the land belonging to Temple has not been acquired or the same is not required to be acquired.
There is no pleading available on record in this regard.
Reference Court has referred the stand of the respondents which is not available on record.

In absence of pleadings, oral .
submission made by or on behalf of a party, is not admissible.
The statement of RW-1 is also not in consonance with the pleadings of reply filed on behalf of respondents, rather it is contrary to the pleadings.
Evidence not supported by pleadings is also of no value.

Therefore, Reference Court has erred in law by putting reliance on oral submissions made on behalf of respondents or considering Sh. Dev. Markanda Ji vs The Collector on 31 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46803689/
2 the evidence which is not supported by pleadings rather contrary to pleadings.

sentences.text: Similarly evidence of appellant placed on record as Ex. PW-3/A to 3/D by leading evidence of PW-3 Trvind Mehta has been discarded without any material available on record to rebut the same.

6. It is undisputed that Award passed by Reference court with respect to other land owners,
compensation wherein was enhanced by Reference Court vide impugned award referred supra, has attained finality, as the same has been accepted and implemented by respondents.

7. Learned counsel for the appellant for claiming entitlement of the appellant on parity for enhancement of compensation like other co- owners, whose land and property has been acquired by common notification, has placed reliance on pronouncement of the Supreme Court in Murali alias Dhananjayan Vs. State of Kerala, reported in (2021) 3 SCC 747.
8.

entities.text: Murali alias Dhananjayan Vs. State of Kerala, reported in (2021) 3 SCC 747
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
From the record, it is evident that land and structure of appellant-temple was acquired by the respondents and the same was never excluded or de-notified, from process of acquisition initiated by issuing Section 4 notification, at any stage, rather compensation payable to the appellant was determined as 6,17,729/-, and was paid 1,98,000/- in lieu of compensation for land and 2,40,105/-
were paid for compensation for structure and 1,31,432/- was paid for compulsory acquisition charges under Section 23(2) of the Act.

9. On completion of acquisition proceedings, and on payment of .
compensation to the property owners, the entire land alongwith structure stands vested in Project Proponent and therefore, plea that acquired structure is standing on the acquired land and has not been removed/dismantled or is used by devotees is meaningless because ownership thereof vests in Project Proponent for acquisition of land and structure thereon.

It is also noticeable that acquisition of land and structure of temple and Inn has never been questioned or assailed by respondents at any point of time, rather acquisition has been accepted by making payment of compensation determined by Land Acquisition Collector.

10. In view of aforesaid discussion, I find that Reference Court has committed material illegality in considering the submissions and evidence on behalf of respondents, which are not supported by pleadings, which were also contrary to the stand taken by respondents in the reply.

Therefore,
appellant is also entitled for enhancement of the value of structure @ 10% in terms of value as determined by Reference Court with respect to other claimants/land owners/structure owners.
Therefore, dismissal of Reference Petition no. 9 of 2007 preferred by appellant, vide impugned Award, is set aside and present appeal is allowed and impugned award is modified accordingly.
Therefore appellant shall be entitled for 10% enhancement in the value of structure/temple and Inn determined by Collector as 2,40,105/-.
Reasons assigned for enhancing 10% value of structure of other co-owners in the impugned Award shall be applicable mutatis mutandis to the claim of appellant also for all intents and purposes.
